research.neighbourhoods_housing: Verified via presidentmovers.ca and zealty.ca real-estate guides: Metrotown is high-rise condo/mixed-use with Metropolis mall and Central Park (90 acres, old-growth forest); Brentwood is mostly condos/towers with '250+ shops, 11 new residential towers' around Brentwood Town Centre SkyTrain; Burnaby Heights has heritage homes and post-war bungalows plus historic Hastings St neon signage; South Burnaby/Edmonds is predominantly single-family and townhomes near the Fraser River, Burnaby Fraser Foreshore Park and Riverway Golf Course.
research.climate: Two sources (climate-data.org, weather-and-climate.com) give slightly different figures, so used ranges rather than false precision: average annual rainfall roughly 2,300mm+, wettest months Nov-Jan, humidity commonly cited 65-85% depending on month/source.
research.strata_law: Verified via BC government (gov.bc.ca) Strata Housing guidance: garage/parking areas in strata buildings are either common property or limited common property (LCP); strata bylaws can restrict what's stored there (furniture, combustibles); exclusive-use rights attach to the owner, not the strata lot, so they don't automatically transfer on resale; Form B Information Certificate plus current bylaws govern the actual rules for a given building. This is general BC provincial guidance, not Burnaby-specific bylaw text -- described it that way, not as a Burnaby-only rule.
research.not_used: Declined to cite specific real-estate price figures (median condo/townhouse prices) since they date quickly and aren't needed to make the storage argument -- used only the verifiable structural fact (eleven towers around Brentwood) for local texture.
